label: SIMULATED, not demand evidence
product: Retro golf rope cap, Ivory, forest-green front embroidery, new unknown brand, $34, mid-November
method: 100 simulated shoppers; each reaction written individually by judgement (no scoring rules); slogan order randomised per shopper; aggregates computed from those reactions.

shoppers.situation: Organising a 12-man Myrtle Beach trip for March, wants matching hats for the group photo
shoppers.dislike_reason: 'On God' isn't how anyone in our group talks; feels borrowed
shoppers.reason: Cart Cousins is literally what we call ourselves; it's a crew name, not a joke that expires.

shoppers.situation: Planning a bachelor-party golf day in Scottsdale
shoppers.dislike_reason: Sounds like a pub quiz team, zero energy
shoppers.reason: Big Tee Energy gets a laugh on the first tee and the groom's mum won't clock it.

shoppers.situation: Runs a 20-year Ryder Cup-style weekend with college friends
shoppers.dislike_reason: No idea what 'it's giving' means and I'm not googling it
shoppers.reason: Most of these read like a 22-year-old wrote them; Cart Cousins is the only one my group would say, and I'd rather have our trip name stitched.

shoppers.situation: Organises a monthly work-friends scramble
shoppers.dislike_reason: Read it three times and still don't know what it means
shoppers.reason: Fairway Function sounds like an event, which is what our scramble is; I'd want reviews before ordering 16.

shoppers.situation: Organises the company golf outing for clients
shoppers.dislike_reason: HR would kill anything that's a play on that phrase
shoppers.reason: Birdies & Banter is the only one I could hand a client without explaining it.

shoppers.situation: Sorting a Vegas golf weekend for 8 mates
shoppers.dislike_reason: Sounds like a family reunion minivan
